rows.published_claim: Tyr and Trp are strongly over-represented in antibody combining sites; Tyr is the single commonest paratope residue.
rows.sources: Mian, Bradwell & Olson 1991; MacCallum, Martin & Thornton 1996; Ramaraj et al. 2012; Peng et al. 2014
rows.our_measurement: Tyr log2 enrichment +1.71 vs general PPI interfaces and +2.70 vs the antibody's own surface; Trp +1.14 / +3.04
rows.note: Recovered on both nulls, so this is selective use of aromatics, not a consequence of antibodies being aromatic-rich overall.

rows.published_claim: Ser, Thr and Gly are commonly listed alongside Tyr/Trp as enriched paratope residues.
rows.sources: MacCallum et al. 1996; Collis et al. 2003; Ramaraj et al. 2012
rows.our_measurement: Ser +1.14 vs PPI but -0.69 vs the antibody's own surface; Thr +0.21 / -0.94; Gly +0.44 / -0.45
rows.note: Enriched relative to general protein interfaces but DEPLETED relative to the antibody's own accessible surface. The apparent enrichment is a property of antibody composition, not of selective paratope usage. Only Tyr and Trp are enriched on both nulls. This distinction is invisible to any study using a single background.

rows.published_claim: CDR-H3 contributes more antigen contacts than any other loop and is the principal determinant of specificity.
rows.sources: Kabat & Wu; MacCallum, Martin & Thornton 1996; Xu & Davis 2000
rows.our_measurement: Fab: H3 = 37.2% of CDR contacts (next: H2 17.7%, L3 17.3%, L2 2.4%). Nanobody: H3 = 65.7%
rows.note: L2 contributes almost nothing, also as reported. Nanobodies push H3 dominance far higher, consistent with the absence of a light chain and a longer H3.

rows.published_claim: Framework residues contribute a minority but non-negligible fraction of antigen contacts.
rows.sources: MacCallum et al. 1996; Sela-Culang, Kunik & Ofran 2013
rows.our_measurement: framework = 21.6% of paratope contacts, stable across Fab/Fv/nanobody (0.209-0.222)

rows.published_claim: Most protein antigenic epitopes are conformational / discontinuous, comprising several sequence segments and roughly 15-25 residues.
rows.sources: Barlow, Edwards & Thornton 1986; Rubinstein et al. 2009; Kringelum et al. 2013; Sela-Culang et al. 2013
rows.our_measurement: median 4 sequence segments, 97.5% of epitopes discontinuous (>=2 segments), median 22 epitope residues
rows.note: Both the segment count and the epitope size fall squarely in the published range.

rows.published_claim: Salt bridges and complementary charge pairing are a conserved feature of protein-protein interfaces.
rows.sources: Barlow & Thornton 1983; Jones & Thornton 1996; Xu, Tsai & Nussinov 1997
rows.our_measurement: K-D, D-K, K-E, R-D, R-E are top-enriched and bootstrap-sign-stable in BOTH arms; salt-bridge fraction is statistically identical (antibody 0.033 vs PPI 0.033, p=0.30) as is opposite-charge pairing (0.051 vs 0.051, p=0.35)
rows.note: Charge chemistry is genuinely universal -- and therefore is NOT what distinguishes antibodies. A negative result worth stating.

rows.published_claim: Typical protein-protein interfaces bury ~1,600 A2 total and involve ~20-30 residues per side; antibody-antigen interfaces sit at the smaller end of the transient range.
rows.sources: Jones & Thornton 1996; Lo Conte, Chothia & Janin 1999; Chakrabarti & Janin 2002
rows.our_measurement: antibody median 59 residue pairs vs PPI 86 (effect -0.31, p=2.8e-13); epitope median 22 residues
rows.note: Antibody interfaces are significantly smaller than general PPI interfaces on every size measure.

rows.published_claim: Antibody-antigen interfaces are less hydrophobic than obligate/homodimeric interfaces and more polar in character.
rows.sources: Jones & Thornton 1996; Lo Conte et al. 1999; Chakrabarti & Janin 2002
rows.our_measurement: apolar-apolar contact fraction antibody 0.145 vs PPI 0.261 (effect -0.52, p=1.4e-33); H-bond fraction 0.253 vs 0.200 (effect +0.44)
rows.note: The largest single physicochemical separations we measure. Antibodies substitute aromatic and H-bond chemistry for hydrophobic burial.

rows.published_claim: Aromatic residues, and cation-pi interactions, are important in antibody recognition.
rows.sources: Gallivan & Dougherty 1999; Ramaraj et al. 2012; Peng et al. 2014
rows.our_measurement: aromatic involvement antibody 0.431 vs PPI 0.306 (effect +0.53); cation-pi 0.056 vs 0.032; functional-group map: aromatic ring <-> ammonium +1.07 antibody-enriched
rows.note: But formal ring-ring stacking is DEPLETED in antibodies (W-Y delta -0.99, Y-Y -0.85, both significant). The aromatic enrichment is aromatics contacting NON-aromatics -- backbone and cations -- not pi-stacking. Frequently blurred in the literature.

rows.topic: What antibodies read on the antigen
rows.published_claim: Antibody recognition is usually described in terms of side-chain complementarity and shape matching.
rows.our_measurement: side-chain-mediated fraction is IDENTICAL in both arms (~0.72, per-residue correlation r=0.981), but the main-chain readout GRAMMAR diverges (cross-arm r=0.135 vs 0.493 for side chains); Tyr phenol -OH to antigen backbone N-H/C=O is +0.56/+0.58 antibody-enriched
rows.note: The distinguishing feature is not how MUCH backbone is read but HOW it is read. We are not aware of this decomposition being reported; it is the study's primary novel claim.

rows.published_claim: Antibody-antigen interfaces are often described as 'ordinary' protein interfaces distinguished mainly by their loop scaffold and lack of co-evolution.
rows.sources: Jones & Thornton 1996; Sundberg & Mariuzza 2002; Ofran et al. 2008
rows.our_measurement: grammar correlation r=0.418 (0.586 with Cys masked; chemical-class r=0.841); permutation test of a single shared grammar: observed r=0.417 vs null 0.798 [0.728, 0.850], p=0.0010
rows.note: Same chemistry at the class level (r=0.84) but formally distinct grammars at residue level (p=0.001). And the difference is NOT the loop scaffold: matching both arms on secondary structure (loop-loop r=0.185) and on CATH fold class does not raise the correlation -- it lowers it, below size-matched nulls.

rows.published_claim: Epitopes are often reported as enriched in loops/turns and in protruding, flexible regions.
rows.sources: Thornton et al. 1986; Rubinstein et al. 2009; Kringelum et al. 2013
rows.our_measurement: epitope loop fraction 0.512 vs PPI partner loop fraction 0.509; paratope loop fraction 0.670 vs PPI probe 0.462
rows.note: Epitopes are NOT structurally unusual: their loop content is indistinguishable from ordinary PPI partner surfaces (0.512 vs 0.509). The loop enrichment is entirely on the PARATOPE side. Claims that epitopes are loop-rich appear to be relative to whole protein rather than to other interfaces.

rows.published_claim: Nanobodies (VHH) rely disproportionately on a long CDR-H3 and can access clefts inaccessible to Fabs.
rows.our_measurement: H3 = 65.7% of nanobody CDR contacts vs 37.2% in Fabs; Fab-vs-nanobody grammar r=0.179, inside the Fab split-half reliability ceiling 0.253 [0.117, 0.370]
rows.verdict: AGREE on architecture, EXTEND on chemistry
rows.note: H3 dominance is confirmed and much stronger in nanobodies. But the two formats' recognition CHEMISTRY is indistinguishable at matched sample size -- different architecture, same grammar.

rows.published_claim: Glycan shields obstruct antibody access to viral antigens; PTMs regulate protein-protein interactions.
rows.sources: Wei et al. 2020 (glycan shield); Nishi, Hashimoto & Panchenko 2011 (PTMs at interfaces)
rows.our_measurement: interfacial glycans: antibody 14.1% vs PPI 5.1% (OR 3.07, p=1.6e-11); interfacial PTMs: antibody 1.6% vs PPI 9.0% (OR 0.16, p=7.3e-11)
rows.verdict: AGREE, and QUANTIFY a double dissociation
rows.note: Antibody interfaces engage glycans ~3x more; PPI interfaces engage PTMs ~6x more. Partly a target-composition effect (viral glycoproteins vs signalling complexes) and stated as such.

rows.published_claim: Antibody-antigen interfaces have lower shape complementarity (~0.64-0.68) than protease-inhibitor or oligomeric interfaces (~0.70-0.76).
rows.note: Required for publication: Lawrence & Colman defined Sc on exactly this comparison, and reviewers will expect it. Our smaller-but-tighter result (closest approach 3.587 vs 3.641 A) makes a specific prediction here, so it is a real test rather than a formality.

rows.published_claim: Binding free energy concentrates in a few 'hot spot' residues, enriched in Trp, Arg and Tyr, surrounded by an occluding O-ring.
rows.note: Burial data from Phase 6a is in place; the analysis is cheap and connects to the most-cited PPI literature.
